introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{2}{x^2 - 1}$,

(a) express $f(x)$ in partial fractions. Hence,

(b) show that $\displaystyle\int_3^5 f(x)\,dx = \ln\left(\frac43\right)$. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)** Since $x^2 - 1 = (x-1)(x+1)$, write

$$\frac{2}{(x-1)(x+1)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{x+1} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2 = A(x+1) + B(x-1).$$

Put $x = 1$: $2 = 2A$, so $A = 1$. Put $x = -1$: $2 = -2B$, so $B = -1$.

$$\boxed{f(x) = \frac{1}{x-1} - \frac{1}{x+1}}$$

**(b)** On $[3, 5]$ we have $x - 1 > 0$ and $x + 1 > 0$, so

$$\int_3^5 f(x)\,dx = \Big[\ln(x-1) - \ln(x+1)\Big]_3^5 = \Big[\ln\frac{x-1}{x+1}\Big]_3^5 = \ln\frac{4}{6} - \ln\frac{2}{4} = \ln\frac23 - \ln\frac12.$$

$$= \ln\left(\frac23 \div \frac12\right) = \ln\frac43.$$

This is the required result. Numerical check: $\ln\tfrac43 = 0.28768$, and the integral evaluated numerically is $0.28768$.

Keep one factor $\sin x$ for $du$, convert the other powers of $\sin$ with $\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x$, and use the substitution $u = \cos x$, $du = -\sin x\,dx$:

$$\int \cos^3 x \sin^3 x\,dx = \int \cos^3 x\,(1 - \cos^2 x)\sin x\,dx = -\int u^3(1 - u^2)\,du = -\int (u^3 - u^5)\,du.$$

$$= -\frac{u^4}{4} + \frac{u^6}{6} + C.$$

$$\boxed{\int \cos^3 x \sin^3 x\,dx = -\frac{\cos^4 x}{4} + \frac{\cos^6 x}{6} + C}$$

Check by differentiating: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(-\dfrac{\cos^4 x}{4} + \dfrac{\cos^6 x}{6}\right) = \cos^3 x\sin x - \cos^5 x \sin x = \cos^3 x\sin x(1 - \cos^2 x) = \cos^3 x \sin^3 x$.

*Equivalent forms.* The substitution $u = \sin x$ gives $\dfrac{\sin^4 x}{4} - \dfrac{\sin^6 x}{6} + C'$; the two answers differ only by a constant ($\tfrac1{12}$), so both are correct. Another route: $\cos^3 x\sin^3 x = \tfrac18\sin^3 2x$.
